requirements.evidence: Data model matches the spec: entities slug unique 'entities_slug_unique' + softDeletes (create_entities_table.php:17-19); memberships with cascade FKs, role default 'employee', stored generated owner_seq and both named unique indexes (create_entity_memberships_table.php:16-26). Policies follow the matrix (EntityPolicy.php, EntityMembershipPolicy.php:32-43). Pick controller checks membership, sets session, logs on 'audit' channel, redirects (EntityPickController.php:17-27). Members: addMember with 'exists:users,email' and duplicate error on email (Members.php:21,39-43), assignRole restricted to manageable roles with error on 'role' (Members.php:58-63), removeMember blocks owner via policy and last manager (Members.php:72-79). Settings: locked entity, unique-except-self slug (Settings.php:116), delete soft-deletes + memberships + session clear (Settings.php:44-59), transfer locks owner, aborts 403 if owner vanished, requires admin of this entity other than caller, demotes then promotes in a transaction (Settings.php:61-89). Routes and lang keys present in both locales. Minor gaps: 'role' validation is a hand-rolled addError rather than a validation rule; targetMembershipId is never validated so the error slot in settings.blade.php is unused.

conventions.evidence: Domain writes (add member, assign role, remove member, save/delete entity, transfer ownership) are done inline in the Livewire components (Members.php:46-49,66,81; Settings.php:41,51-52,85-86) instead of app/Actions/* classes that authorize inside, which the conventions require. Settings uses a rules() method rather than #[Validate] attributes (allowed by the Livewire policy but not the stated project pattern). Positives: policies used for all authorization, #[Fillable] set on both models, migrations with reversible down(), reused <x-form-field>/<x-button> components, docs/database-schema.md and CHANGELOG.md updated.

security.evidence: Every public action authorizes server-side (Members.php:33,56,71; Settings.php:37,46,63); action parameters resolved scoped to the locked entity and 403 otherwise (Members.php:92-98, Settings.php:72-75); entity property is #[Locked] in all three components; all output escaped with {{ }}; mass assignment restricted. Small gaps: targetMembershipId is a public unvalidated property (mitigated by the scoped lookup); no rate limiting on destructive delete/transfer; a hard-coded APP_KEY committed to phpunit.xml:29 (test-only, but a secret-looking value in the repo).

tests.evidence: Six Pest files cover schema/indexes, the DB-level single-owner and duplicate constraints (EntityModelTest.php), the policy matrix (EntityPolicyTest.php), pick incl. 403 with untouched session and audit log (EntityPickTest.php), dashboard owner-only settings link and 403 with session pointing elsewhere (EntityDashboardTest.php), members add/duplicate/unknown/employee-403/owner-role error/cross-entity param tamper/owner removal/last manager (EntityMembersTest.php), and settings save/slug uniqueness/delete/transfer happy path and invalid targets (EntitySettingsTest.php). Missing: a tamper test that setting the #[Locked] entity is rejected, the 'owner row vanished' 403 path of transfer, unauthorized calls to save/delete/transfer actions themselves, and English-locale text assertions.

simplicity.evidence: Lean, direct code; enum + scopes are minimal. Some duplication: the identical isManager() helper in EntityPolicy.php:45-52 and EntityMembershipPolicy.php:44-51; Members::addMember authorizes via a throwaway `new EntityMembership(['entity_id' => ...])` (Members.php:33) where the existing EntityPolicy::update would express the intent directly.

readability.evidence: Clear names, short methods, PHPDoc on relations and policies. Minor: fully-qualified `\App\Models\UserRole` in members.blade.php:41,52; `@error('targetMembershipId')` block (settings.blade.php:47-49) can never trigger; transfer() closure captures copies of properties unnecessarily (Settings.php:65-68).

scope.evidence: Nearly everything serves the task and out-of-scope items (onboarding, switcher, middleware, navbar) were not built. Unrelated edit: adding a hard-coded APP_KEY to phpunit.xml:29.

issues.explanation: Domain writes (add/assign/remove member, save/delete entity, ownership transfer) are implemented inline in Livewire components instead of app/Actions/* use-case classes that authorize internally, as the conventions require.
No tamper test that the #[Locked] entity cannot be swapped from the client, and no test for the transfer 403 when the owner row has vanished, both explicit requirements of the task/Livewire policy.
Public $targetMembershipId has no validation rule; it is safe only because of the scoped lookup, and the @error slot in the view is consequently dead.
Commits a hard-coded APP_KEY to phpunit.xml, an unrelated configuration change that puts a key-like secret in the repository.
The role check is a hand-rolled addError with validation.in instead of a validation rule (e.g. Rule::enum/in via validate), diverging from the project's validation pattern.
The isManager() helper is duplicated across both policies.
Authorizing addMember through a throwaway new EntityMembership is indirect; authorizing 'update' on the entity would read more clearly.
Fully qualified \App\Models\UserRole references in the Blade view instead of passing values from the component.

review.summary: The change implements the entity/membership data model with a DB-enforced single owner, both policies, the pick route with audit log, and the dashboard, members and settings Livewire pages, with server-side authorization, locked entity props and a broad Pest suite. It is functionally solid and secure, but domain writes bypass the required app/Actions layer, some Livewire tamper/owner-vanished tests are missing, and an unrelated APP_KEY was committed to phpunit.xml, so it needs changes before merging.
